keyword_metrics.source: No Search Console, Google Keyword Planner, or validated third-party keyword export was supplied for this candidate.
keyword_metrics.note: Search terms are hypotheses only; no volume, difficulty, or demand is asserted.

search_intent.intent: Unmeasured country-specific research hypothesis: interpret a defined Eurostat Germany employment indicator as broad context, not as evidence of executive vacancy demand.
evidence: Eurostat's 2026 Q2 quarterly dataset provides a Germany-specific seasonally adjusted employment-rate observation for ages 20 to 64.
Eurostat's quarterly labour-market article distinguishes employment rates from labour-market slack.

intended_audience: Senior executives and candidates researching the German employment market.
geographic_relevance: Germany only for the numeric observation; EU-wide context is clearly labeled and not generalized to Germany.

competitor_research.name: Germany-localized candidate-facing search results and direct market-guide competitors
competitor_research.finding: A current Germany-localized search-results review and direct market-guide comparison was not performed.

commercial_relevance: Potential country-specific candidate research resource only if a distinct user need, demand, overlap and KOV serviceability are later established. Eurostat employment data do not establish commercial value or KOV capability.
unique_content_purpose: Explain the exact population, age-band, quarter, seasonal-adjustment setting and denominator of a sourced Germany employment-rate observation and distinguish it from labour-market slack and executive hiring evidence.
duplication_and_cannibalisation_assessme: The existing executive job-search resource is jurisdiction-neutral. This draft is narrowly based on a dated Germany-specific Eurostat observation and its statistical metadata. Full Germany page overlap, SERP and demand review remain pending.

authoritative_sources.source_type: Official EU quarterly labour statistics dataset
authoritative_sources.title: Employment and labour force by sex and age — quarterly data (LFSI_EMP_Q)
authoritative_sources.research_use_and_limit: Used for Germany's seasonally adjusted total employment rate for ages 20 to 64 in 2026 Q2 (81.5%), measured as a percentage of total population. This is a broad labour-force indicator, not executive vacancies, compensation or appointment prospects.

authoritative_sources.title: EU labour market — quarterly statistics
authoritative_sources.research_use_and_limit: Used for the distinction between employment rate and labour-market slack. EU-level findings are not presented as Germany-specific executive demand.

content_status: Source-bounded Germany market research guide implemented in noindex staging with one dated Eurostat indicator and explicit scope limitations.
